code_facts: ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-10-03 — this read "8+ published audits across the Maple v2 corpus; $1M bug bounty" and BOTH figures overstated, against this file's own `assurance` block measured the same day. The bounty is the Immunefi MAPLE program, maximum USD 500,000 (version read 2026-04-21, 43 listed assets) — not $1M. "8+" is a count of Maple protocol engagements, not of engagements covering this pool, and the Dec-2022 and Jun-2023 reviews predate syrupUSDC entirely. [security_analyst measurement]
ERC-4626 standard vault on a multi-year battle-tested MapleGlobals/PoolManager codebase; ~3-year clean record on the Syrup product line, zero principal losses. [published document]

⚠️ Upgrades are bounded to REGISTERED implementations: MapleProxyFactory gates registerImplementation / enableUpgradePath / setDefaultVersion behind onlyGovernor, so three keys buy a rollback to a Maple-published version, not new code. [riskAnalyst assessment]

⚠️ That cap does NOT reach the exit. The redemption-queue powers on the pause layer — not processing, and flipping a holder to manual withdrawal — need no implementation at all. [riskAnalyst assessment]

⚠️ Maple attests the custody EOAs are MPC wallets under policy controls (2026-05-04). CREDITED for key-compromise cost and NOT credited against the liveness path — MPC protects the key from theft, not the holder from the operator declining to act. [riskAnalyst assessment]

⚠️ The attestation is NOT on-chain-verifiable: eth_getCode == 0x rules out a Safe but cannot distinguish MPC from a single key. Do not read walk field `threshold: 1` as a measured compromise cost on these holders. [riskAnalyst assessment]

contract.provenance_note: ⚠️ SOURCE-OF-RECORD RESTORED 2026-09-14. This file was recreated in riskAnalyst/data/axes/ from the copy serving at backing-monitor/data/, which had been the ONLY copy since 2026-09-07/08. ⚠️ HOW IT GOT THERE: it was authored, synced, committed on the consumer side, and then ceased to exist on the producer side -- it has NEVER been in riskAnalyst's git history at any path. Three gaps let that happen and each is recorded so none is mistaken for the others: (1) the axis-5 spec's ownership table gives the AUTHORITY half a source AND a destination (security_analyst/topology/... -> backing-monitor/data/...) and gives OUR half only a destination, so it never named an authoring location; (2) sync_and_push.sh's SLUGS x SUFFIXES x ROOTS loop warns on COLLISION and on an unpublished marker but has NO branch for ABSENCE, so a registered slug whose source has vanished is silent -- the script's own comments argue against exactly this twice, including 'a missing source must be LOUD' and 'the failure was silent because the stale copy was committed'; (3) riskAnalyst's pre-commit hook exited unless assets/*.md was staged, so nothing guarded data/axes/ at all until 2026-09-14. ✅ CONTENT IS UNCHANGED FROM THE SERVING COPY AND THE SCORE WAS GATED BEFORE RESTORING: structural_score was checked against the report's frontmatter and matched for all seven. NOTHING WAS RE-DERIVED -- this restores a source of record, it does not re-open a judgement.

assurance.headline: ⚠️⚠️ '8+ TOTAL AUDITS ACROSS THE V1 AND V2 LIFECYCLE' IS NOT EIGHT syrupUSDC AUDITS, AND THE REASON IS TEMPORAL RATHER THAN MERELY INHERITED: syrupUSDC DID NOT EXIST when the three December 2022 V2 launch reviews or the two June 2023 reviews occurred. Those engagements reviewed reusable pool, manager, withdrawal and loan code later used by syrupUSDC. ⚠️ An audit cannot have covered an asset that post-dates it.

assurance.upgrade_path_and_admin_roles: ⚠️⚠️ NOT COVERED, AND ONE REPORT DISCLAIMS IT EXPLICITLY. No reviewed report audits the live syrupUSDC authority topology — in particular the TWO DISTINCT poolDelegate-derived EOA control paths recorded in the admin walk. Reports examine access-control LOGIC, and the September 2025 pair examine GovernorTimelock roles, but neither establishes who controls the live privileged addresses. ⚠️ AND TRAIL OF BITS EXPLICITLY STATES it reviewed the V2 upgrade mechanism only to understand it and 'did not look for security flaws.'
assurance.prose_correction: ⚠️ THIS REPORT SAID: 'Both Spearbit and Trail of Bits on the v2/Syrup contracts is a notable positive — the audit profile of a well-funded, security-conscious protocol.' Trail of Bits DISCLAIMED looking for security flaws in the upgrade mechanism, so citing it as a positive on that surface is wrong, not merely unscoped.
